claims.text: Keycloak stores its users in its own database, so a PostgreSQL transaction in Đơn Hàng's database cannot include or undo creating the account. No single transaction covers both.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0033 @ stage-4 lines 25-26; saas-platform-design-review.md lines 56-57; PostgreSQL 17 docs: Transactions, PREPARE TRANSACTION; Keycloak docs: Configuring the database

claims.text: Path: the sign-up form sends a sign-up, the API writes one sign-up row, and a background job runs each step keyed by the sign-up's id.

Sign-up steps: 1 shops row pending with the chosen plan; 2 first staff account in Keycloak with role staff and the shop; 3 welcome message to the outbox, Notifications emails at least once; 4 shop active.

Every step checks whether it is already done before acting, using the sign-up's id; the review names two examples (a shops row for this sign-up id; the account exists) and not those of steps 3-4. So running the job again from the start is safe.
Any step that keeps failing leaves the shop pending, shown to Đơn Hàng's own employees by role; the shop is never half open.
ADR 0033's header says nothing is built at stage-4: no sign-up, plan or shop-settings code in the repository.

ADR 0033: shops row records plan, settings, status pending/active/leaving; a plan is numbers (concurrent-read share, staff accounts, chat on/off, data kept, assumed). ADR 0016 caps each shop's part of a shared limit; a plan sets only the cap's size, a ceiling: unused share stays for others.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0033 @ stage-4 lines 34-37; saas-platform-design-review.md lines 88, 109; multi-shop-open-requirements.md line 16

claims.text: ADR 0026: the mapping table (which database holds each shop) is a column of shops, the row that also records the plan; each Pod keeps it in memory for a short time. ADR 0033: a plan change takes effect when that copy expires.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0033-cua-hang-tu-dang-ky-goi-la-du-lieu.md @ stage-4 lines 37-38; docs/adr/0026-cua-hang-lon-chuyen-sang-database-rieng.md @ stage-4 lines 36-41; ADR 0033 line 34 (shops row records plan)

claims.text: A plan's features are settings read from the shop's data and live with the plan; a release flag (feature-flags.md), a feature flag used to roll a feature out, is removed once its feature is on for every customer.
A shop picks by name among Brand values built into the app that passed the contrast tests; adding a brand is an app release; no free colours and no logo.
brand.dart ships one constant Brand, donHangBrand; its comment says each 'on' colour keeps a contrast of at least 4.5:1 with its background, tested by the accessibility checks.
The customer's app reads the shop's name, settings and brand name through the API, then uses the built-in brand of the same name.
If Keycloak fails, sign-up stops at step 2 and the shop waits as pending; shops already running are unaffected.

Rejected: opening by hand (breaks driver 1, each opening a chance of error) and one combined transaction (Keycloak is another owner). Trade-off points: built-in brand vs free colour; plan as ceiling vs reservation (unused share stays for others, higher plan gets no guaranteed room).

ADR 0033 review conditions (events that reopen it): shops need free colours or a logo (contrast tests must then run on shop data); sign-ups per day grow until the saga job is a bottleneck; a plan needs a reservation instead of a ceiling. The review plans a new ADR for free colours or logo.
Estimate: about five sign-ups a day (assumed); SA-1 asks a shop to open within ten minutes (assumed).
Notifications sends the welcome email at least once: never lost, sometimes sent twice.

When sign-ups must work across owners with no shared transaction, a saga whose steps check before acting fits; built-in brands fit when readability must hold for every shop; free colours fit only once contrast tests run on shop data.
Keycloak realm donhang defines the realm role staff.
